t: Marine Engine: Hull Speed Desk — Simple
name: Marine Engine: Hull Speed Desk — Simple
title: Marine Engine: Hull Speed Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Displacement hulls have a speed limit: v ≈ 1.34 × √L (knots, L in feet). The desk computes the hull speed per waterline — a 36-ft hull tops at 8 knots. The formula is the wave physics, not an opinion.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Hull speed for 36 ft waterline = 8.04 knots. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.

signature_version: Signature version: the deterministic hull desk — the chapter's Marine Engine as the speed target, with the speculative framing labeled concept.

safety: No hazard; the failure mode is a displacement hull pushed past its wave.
